8:["$","$L13",null,{"data":{"chapterId":5,"verseId":3,"chapterTitle":"Examination of Elements","totalVerses":8,"verseData":{"id":"v5_3","number":3,"title":"Characteristics Cannot Arise Anywhere","sanskrit":{"text":"na alakṣaṇe lakṣaṇasya pravṛttir na ca lakṣaṇe | lakṣaṇalakṣaṇābhyāṃ ca nānyatrāpi pravartate ||","transliteration":"na alakṣaṇe lakṣaṇasya pravṛttir na ca lakṣaṇe | lakṣaṇalakṣaṇābhyāṃ ca nānyatrāpi pravartate","translation":"Neither in the uncharacterised nor in the characterised does a characteristic arise. Nor does it arise in something different from these two."},"philosophy":{"insight":"Characteristics cannot arise ANYWHERE through inherent processes: not in an uncharacterised thing (none exist, per v.2), not in an already characterised thing (it already has the characteristic), and not in some third thing (what would that be?). All three options for independent arising are exhausted. This is a complete trilemma proving the impossibility of independently arising characteristics.","madhyamaka":"Garfield: this is a classic Madhyamaka trilemma — exhausting all logical possibilities for the inherent arising of characteristics. The structure mirrors Ch. 2's analysis of motion (not in the moved, not in the unmoved, not in the being-moved). Siderits/Katsura: the \"something different from these two\" clause blocks the escape route of positing a third substrate (like a Platonic realm) where characteristics might independently reside. Candrakīrti: this verse demonstrates that lakṣaṇa (characteristic) has no svabhāva (inherent existence) because no coherent account of its arising can be given.","quantum":"Quantum Measurement and the Absence of Pre-Existing Values: In quantum mechanics, measurement outcomes (characteristics) don't pre-exist in the unmeasured system (uncharacterised), don't need to \"arise\" in an already-measured system (characterised), and don't come from a separate hidden-variable realm (third option — ruled out by Bell's theorem). The trilemma of where measurement outcomes \"come from\" is the quantum version of Nāgārjuna's puzzle.","bridge":"Both describe a trilemma about where properties arise. Nāgārjuna: not in the uncharacterised, not in the characterised, not in a third thing. Quantum measurement: not in the unmeasured state, not in the already-measured state, not in hidden variables. All three options fail in both frameworks, pointing to dependent arising / contextual emergence.","accessible":"Where does the \"redness\" of a tomato come from? Not from a \"bare tomato\" (none exist). Not from a \"red tomato\" (it's already red). Not from some separate \"redness realm.\" The redness arises WITH the tomato in its growth process — dependently, not from any independent source. Quantum measurements are similar: the result doesn't come from anywhere independently.","twoTruths":"Conventionally, we say \"the tomato turns red\" as if redness arrives from somewhere. Ultimately, redness and tomato co-arise within conditions (sunlight, pigment chemistry, observer perception). The \"arriving\" language is conventional shorthand.","commonMisconception":"NOT saying characteristics don't arise — they obviously do. Saying characteristics don't arise INDEPENDENTLY from any pre-existing substrate. They arise dependently, co-emergently, within a web of conditions. The mechanism of arising is dependent, not inherent."},"quantumResonance":{"concept":"Quantum Measurement Trilemma / No Pre-Existing Values","score":85,"strength":"High","explanation":"Measurement outcomes don't come from the unmeasured state, the already-measured state, or hidden variables. The trilemma of \"where do outcomes come from?\" parallels the trilemma of characteristic-arising.","caveat":"Both trilemmas have the same logical structure (three options exhausted). The quantum version concerns specific measurement outcomes; Nāgārjuna's concerns all characteristics generally."},"animation":{"geometry":"Trilemma — Three Failed Paths","anchor":"Three doors labelled \"Uncharacterised,\" \"Already Characterised,\" \"Third Thing.\" A glowing characteristic-orb tries to enter each door. Door 1: opens to empty void (no bare entities exist). Door 2: opens to a mirror reflecting the orb back (already has it). Door 3: opens to nothing (no third realm). All three doors fail. Then the orb and its entity co-arise in the center.","texture":"Doors: Dark wood with amber labels. Orb: Glowing golden. Void: Black emptiness. Mirror: Silver reflective. Center co-arising: Vivid blue-gold emergence.","mood":"Systematic elimination → deadlock → co-arising resolution","colors":["#F59E0B","#6B7280","#3B82F6","#0F172A"],"orchestration":{"start":"Three doors stand in space. A glowing orb approaches.","click":"Click each door to test. Door 1: void (no target). Door 2: mirror (already done). Door 3: nothing (no realm). Hover over co-arising: \"Dependent arising — the only option.\""},"controls":{"rotation":{"default":true,"speed":0.3},"speed":{"default":50,"min":0,"max":100},"complexity":{"default":60,"min":0,"max":100},"zoom":{"default":100,"min":50,"max":200},"colorPicker":true,"autoRevealToggle":true},"r3fTechniques":["drei Box for door geometry with text labels","MeshPhysicalMaterial sphere for characteristic orb","Custom portal shader for door openings","Mirror reflection using Environment map","Bloom post-processing for co-arising glow","useSpring for door animations and orb movements"],"camera":{"position":[0,2,10],"fov":50,"autoRotate":true},"fps":60,"performanceNotes":"<250MB memory, 60 FPS. Three door meshes + one sphere + shader effects.","visualBridge":"The three failing doors and the co-arising resolution encode the trilemma: characteristics can't arise independently anywhere, so they must arise dependently.","educationalGoal":"User systematically tests all three options for where characteristics arise and sees all three fail, leading to the conclusion of dependent co-arising."},"deeperDive":[{"q":"Why is this a trilemma?","a":"A trilemma presents three options and shows all are untenable. Here: (1) characteristics arise in uncharacterised things — impossible, none exist. (2) They arise in already-characterised things — pointless, they're already there. (3) They arise in something else entirely — what would that be? No third substrate is coherent. All three options for inherent arising fail.","realLifeExample":"Where does a wave come from? Not from still water (the wave would need to create itself). Not from an already-waving surface (it's already there). Not from some wave-realm. It arises from conditions — wind, gravity, surface tension — dependently."},{"q":"How does this connect to the quantum measurement problem?","a":"Quantum measurement faces the same trilemma: (1) The outcome can't pre-exist in the unmeasured state (that's hidden variables, ruled out by Bell). (2) It can't arise in an already-measured state (that's already done). (3) It can't come from a separate realm. So where does it come from? It arises contextually in the measurement interaction — dependently, not from any pre-existing source.","realLifeExample":"Where does the \"heads\" come from when you flip a coin? Not from the unflipped coin (it's not yet heads). Not from an already-flipped coin (that's already settled). Not from some coin-realm. It arises in the flipping process — from conditions."},{"q":"What is the \"third thing\" Nāgārjuna eliminates?","a":"It's any proposed external substrate, realm, or entity that is neither the characterised object nor the characteristic itself — something in which characteristics might independently reside. This blocks Platonic-style escape routes (a \"realm of forms\" where properties exist independently). It also blocks the idea of a divine mind or cosmic consciousness in which properties pre-exist.","deeper":"Siderits/Katsura: this clause targets any view that posits a separate ontological level (like Sāṃkhya's pradhāna or Nyāya's inherence relation) as the independent source of properties."},{"q":"How does this relate to Bell's theorem?","a":"Bell's theorem (1964) showed that no local hidden variable theory can reproduce all quantum predictions. This eliminates option (3) — there's no hidden \"third thing\" that pre-determines measurement outcomes. The quantum measurement trilemma is formally analogous to Nāgārjuna's: properties don't pre-exist, aren't redundantly re-created, and don't come from a hidden realm.","realLifeExample":"Bell proved there's no \"cheat sheet\" behind quantum measurements. Nāgārjuna proved there's no hidden substrate behind characteristics. Both say: properties arise in relationship, not from independent sources."},{"q":"Does this prove emptiness or just mutual dependence?","a":"Both — they're the same thing. Mutual dependence IS emptiness. If characteristics can't arise independently (from any of the three sources), then they lack inherent existence (svabhāva). What lacks inherent existence is empty. The trilemma proves emptiness by exhausting all possibilities for independent arising.","realLifeExample":"If a business can't succeed alone (no customers), can't succeed with competitors doing the same thing (redundant), and can't succeed by magic (no third option) — then its success DEPENDS on the right conditions. Dependence = its \"inherent success\" is empty."},{"q":"How does this trilemma mirror Ch. 2's motion analysis?","a":"Ch. 2: motion doesn't occur in the moved path (already past), the unmoved path (hasn't started), or some third path. Ch. 5: characteristics don't arise in the uncharacterised (none exist), the characterised (already done), or a third thing. Same logical structure applied to different targets — showing the method is universal.","deeper":"Garfield: the consistency of the trilemma structure across chapters demonstrates that the method isn't ad hoc — it's a systematic analysis applicable to any domain."}],"quiz":{"beginner":{"question":"Where can characteristics arise, according to Nāgārjuna?","options":["A) In uncharacterised things","B) Nowhere independently — not in the uncharacterised, not in the characterised, not in a third thing. They arise dependently.","C) In already characterised things","D) In a separate realm of forms"],"correct":"B","explanation":"All three options for independent arising fail. Characteristics arise dependently, co-emergently with their entities, not from any independent source."},"intermediate":{"question":"How does the quantum measurement trilemma parallel this verse?","options":["A) Quantum outcomes always pre-exist","B) Outcomes don't pre-exist in unmeasured states (1), aren't redundant in measured states (2), and don't come from hidden variables (3, ruled out by Bell) — they arise contextually, like characteristics arising dependently","C) There is no quantum parallel","D) Hidden variables solve the measurement problem"],"correct":"B","explanation":"Quantum measurement faces the same trilemma: outcomes can't come from the unmeasured state, the already-measured state, or hidden variables. They arise contextually — dependent co-arising."},"advanced":{"question":"How does eliminating the \"third thing\" block Platonic-style arguments?","options":["A) It doesn't address Platonic arguments","B) By showing that no separate realm (Forms, pradhāna, divine mind) can serve as an independent source of properties — characteristics can't pre-exist in any third substrate","C) Plato agrees with Nāgārjuna","D) The third thing is the correct answer"],"correct":"B","explanation":"Nāgārjuna's third clause eliminates any proposed external realm or substrate where properties might independently reside — blocking Platonic Forms, Sāṃkhya's pradhāna, and any other \"third thing\" escape route."}},"verseText":"Neither in the uncharacterised nor in the characterised does a characteristic arise. Nor does it arise in something different from these two.","madhyamakaConcept":"Garfield: this is a classic Madhyamaka trilemma — exhausting all logical possibilities for the inherent arising of characteristics. Siderits/Katsura: the \"something different from these two\" clause blocks the escape route of positing a third substrate (like a Platonic realm) where characteristics might independently reside.
